prompt: From a spot $200$ ft from the base of a building, a surveyor whose instrument sits $5$ ft above the ground measures the angle of elevation to the roof as $55^\circ$. How tall is the building? Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.
hint: The triangle starts at the instrument, not at the ground — so the trig gives you only part of the height.

hints.text: The triangle starts at the instrument, not at the ground — so the trig gives you only part of the height.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: from $100$ ft away at $45^\circ$ with the instrument $2$ ft up, the rise is $100\tan 45^\circ = 100$ ft and the building is $100 + 2 = 102$ ft. Trig gives the rise; the instrument height is added last.
First find the rise above eye level: $\tan 55^\circ = \frac{x}{200}$, so $x = 200\tan 55^\circ$.
$x \approx 285.6$ ft above the instrument, then add the $5$ ft instrument height: $285.6 + 5 = 290.6$ ft.

explanation: The right triangle has its horizontal leg $200$ ft and its vertical leg running from instrument height up to the roof.
That is the height ABOVE the instrument, so add the instrument height: $285.6 + 5 = 290.6$ ft.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw the picture in two pieces
steps: Sketch the building and draw a horizontal line at the height of the instrument, 5 ft up.
Everything above that line is the triangle you can solve with tangent: about $285.6$ ft.
Everything below it is the 5 ft slab you must add back, giving $290.6$ ft total.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is $285.6$ ft — correct trigonometry, but it measures the building from the surveyor's eye rather than from the ground.

Whenever a problem bothers to tell you an eye height, instrument height, or cliff height, it is telling you there is a piece to add at the end. Finish by asking: "height above what?" and add whatever is underneath.
